key_insight: Minimizing joint MMD can fail to recover accurate conditional distributions, while directly targeting conditional MMD yields guarantees for triangular transport models.
engineering_relevance: Conditional generators should use objectives aligned with conditional sampling accuracy rather than rely on joint distribution matching alone.
method: Express joint and conditional MMD criteria as quadratic energies of conditional mean embedding residuals.
Analyze a conditional-loss surrogate computable from joint target samples and reference samples.
Derive non-asymptotic error bounds and study joint MMD with concentrating Gaussian conditioning kernels.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical inconsistency results and error bounds separating approximation, estimation, and reference sampling errors, with dimension-independent fast rates in the parametric setting.
watch_item: Concentrating Gaussian kernels make joint MMD approximate a density-reweighted conditional criterion, but the resulting guarantee suffers from the conditioning dimension.
paper_title: On the Error Analysis of Triangular Transport Maps for Conditional Generation via MMD-based Objectives
